name: Triage and act on a bug report
description: Classify-And-Act: one triage context banks a severity verdict as structured output, guarded edges route exactly one remediation branch (with an else edge for the severities no branch names), and a report context fans the outcome back in.

charter.mission: Triage one incoming bug report, act on it down exactly one remediation path, and report what was decided and done.
nonGoals: Fixing defects the report does not describe
Re-triaging after a branch has started

invariants.statement: The triage verdict reaches the workflow only as the triage context's captured structured output. Prose in the summary, a commit message, or a shared document never selects a branch.
Exactly one remediation branch acts on a report. A branch that was not selected does no work and leaves no commits behind.
The report describes the branch that actually ran and names the severity that selected it, so the decision is legible without reading the execution's routing state.

tasks.title: Classify the report's severity
tasks.instructions:
Read the bug report named by the rank-1 source of truth. Reproduce it if the steps allow, and note what you observed. Then classify it as exactly one of: 'blocker' (users are broken now, or data is at risk), 'defect' (wrong behavior on the normal path, with a workaround or limited blast radius), 'enhancement' (the software behaves as designed and the report asks for more), or 'not-a-bug' (the report is a misunderstanding, a duplicate, or not reproducible). Your final output must be the structured verdict: the severity plus a rationale citing the evidence you gathered. Do not start any remediation work — the verdict alone selects which branch runs next.

You are read-only, which is what makes that boundary mechanical rather than a rule you are asked to keep: you have no worktree and you will make no commit, so the verdict is your entire delivery.

tasks.title: Ship the smallest correct fix
tasks.instructions:
The report was triaged as a blocker. Write a regression test that reproduces the reported failure and confirm it fails, then make the smallest change that makes it pass. Do not refactor beyond the fix. Run the touched module's tests and typecheck before completing.

Your captured output carries the triage `severity` VERBATIM alongside your outcome. The reporter downstream is two hops from the classifier, so the severity it reports is the one you pass along — copy it exactly rather than restating it.

tasks.title: Fix the defect at its root cause
tasks.instructions:
The report was triaged as a defect. Identify the root cause before changing anything and state it in your summary. Add a failing behavior-level test, implement the minimum fix, then run the touched module's tests and typecheck.

Your captured output carries the triage `severity` VERBATIM alongside your outcome. The reporter downstream is two hops from the classifier, so the severity it reports is the one you pass along — copy it exactly rather than restating it.

tasks.title: Record the report for the backlog
tasks.instructions:
The report was triaged as an enhancement, as not-a-bug, or as a severity no remediation branch claims. Record it for the backlog: the report itself, the triage rationale, and the reason no code change was made. Change no production code.

Your captured output carries the triage `severity` VERBATIM alongside your outcome. The reporter downstream is two hops from the classifier, so the severity it reports is the one you pass along — copy it exactly rather than restating it.

tasks.title: Summarize the decision and the work
tasks.instructions:
Summarize what happened: the severity, the branch that ran because of it, and what that branch changed or deliberately left alone. All three are in the branch's output in the "Inputs from upstream" section — it carries the triage severity verbatim, because the classifier is two hops upstream of you and only direct predecessors are injected. The upstream inputs section shows you the branch that ran; branches that were not taken appear there as skipped, and you should not describe work on them.

You are read-only. You have no worktree and you will make no commit, so your captured output is your entire delivery: name the severity, the branch context id that actually ran, and the outcome.
